audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 3 and 4-5 were 'Skill' and Level 6 / First item were given to Dr. Mundo, while whys[2] through whys[5] hand every one of those stages to Maokai and only whys[6] flips it.
audit.why: Packet chart is Maokai for Levels 1 through First item and Dr. Mundo at 2+ items. That is the correct scaling-tank shape for a 52.34% win rate over 705 games — Mundo loses the lane and wins the game.
audit.corrected: Maokai x6, Dr. Mundo at 2+ items — ratings 3/4/4/4/4/4/7, with the Level 3 through First item why-text rewritten so it stops arguing Mundo's case on Maokai's stages.

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldowns anywhere; Twisted Advance was listed as 11s.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10s — 11s is its rank-4 value, not what you face in lane. Bramble Smash is 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, Sapling Toss 18/17/16/15/14s at 1100 range, Nature's Grasp 130/110/90s.
audit.corrected: Spikes and the cooldown block now use rank-1 numbers, which is what the player actually sees while the lane is being decided.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sapling Toss is written '(W... E)' — a literal garbled slot. Bramble Smash is called his W; it is his Q. Two fields and a wants-line tell you to escape roots with 'E Blunt Force Trauma'. Twisted Advance's untargetability is never mentioned.
audit.why: Sapling Toss is E, Bramble Smash is Q. Blunt Force Trauma is a targeted slam with an auto-attack reset — Dr. Mundo has no dash and cannot escape anything with it, which is precisely why Nature's Grasp's wall is dangerous. Twisted Advance makes Maokai UNTARGETABLE while dashing, so damage spent into the dash is thrown away. And Mundo's passive resists the first immobilizing effect — that is what eats the W root, dropping a canister you must walk over to cash.
audit.corrected: Fix the slots, delete the escape-with-E advice in all three places, state the untargetable dash, and route the root into the passive-canister plan.

audit.why: suspectNames flagged "Heart Zapper's" in spikes[2] — Heart Zapper is Mundo's real W name, false positive from the possessive.

edits.before: Full kit online and your passive shrugs the first CC. Cleaver poke plus E-empowered swats start the grind; never brawl while Twisted Advance (Root) is up.
edits.after: Twisted Advance (14s at rank 1) goes untargetable mid-dash, so anything you throw into it is wasted. Wait the dash out, then answer once he actually lands.

edits.before: Q ranks make the cleaver chunk real HP and your passive regen ramps. Maokai must kill you through the sustain or watch you out-scale — most can't.
edits.after: Sapling Toss reaches 1100 and zones the whole wave, and Bramble Smash knocks you out of every trade. Farm what is safe; stay out of sapling range.

edits.before: Maximum Dosage online — dives and all-ins flip when you press R mid-fight and regen half your HP. Force Maokai to commit, then out-last the commit.
edits.after: Nature's Grasp (130s at rank 1) plus a jungler is a dive, not a duel — Maximum Dosage does not heal you out of a root wall. Give the wave up.

edits.before: Heartsteel timing — every proc widens the HP gap and your cleavers start hurting. Stand in the wave and dare Maokai to trade into the regen.
edits.after: One item isn't enough — Sap Magic refunds him every time he casts or is hit by a spell. Buy Grievous Wounds before you trade into it again.

edits.before: Maokai's Sapling Toss (W... E) zones your farm and his Bramble Smash (W) knockback plus passive Sap Magic sustain let him out-trade and refuse to be pushed off. His saplings burn your green health every time you step to CS. Don't try to all-in — his sustain and roots reset the trade in his favour. Just farm through it.
edits.after: Maokai's Sapling Toss (E) zones your farm from 1100 range, and Bramble Smash (Q) knockback plus passive Sap Magic sustain let him refuse to be pushed off. Saplings burn your green bar every time you step up to CS. Don't all-in — his sustain and roots reset the trade in his favour. Just farm through it.

edits.before: Maokai's R Nature's Grasp is a long root wave that sets up a jungle dive, and his W Twisted Advance root locks you for a full combo. Your R Maximum Dosage heals, but rooted-in-place you eat sapling burn plus jungler damage. Hold E Blunt Force Trauma to escape after the root breaks and don't overextend when his jungle is missing.
edits.after: Nature's Grasp (R, 130s at rank 1) is a long root wall that sets up a jungle dive, and Twisted Advance (W, 14s at rank 1) turns him UNTARGETABLE mid-dash, so burst spent into it is thrown away. Your passive eats that first root and drops a canister — walk over it. You have no dash, so Flash is for the wall, not the damage.

edits.before: The tide starts turning: with HP items your health pool outgrows his sapling percent-damage and his sustain stops mattering. You can survive his root-combo and W Heart Zapper's grey health recovers the burn. Start walking him down once your tank stats are online.
edits.after: The tide starts turning: with HP items your pool outgrows sapling burn and Sap Magic stops mattering. Heart Zapper (W) banks a slice of the damage he does to you and pays it back when the burst lands — recast it on him, never on empty air, and start walking him down.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 stay his. His constant sapling poke plus root pressure win every reset trade, and at 6 his R Nature's Grasp and W Twisted Advance set up hard jungle dives. Hold E Blunt Force Trauma to break away once a root ends, and don't overextend with his jungler unaccounted for.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 stay his. Constant sapling poke plus root pressure win every reset trade, and at 6 Nature's Grasp and Twisted Advance set up hard jungle dives. Blunt Force Trauma is a slam, not a dash — you cannot break away with it, so hold Flash and never overextend with his jungler unaccounted for.

edits.before: Escape his W/R roots with E Blunt Force Trauma before the combo lands
edits.after: Let your passive eat his first root, then grab the canister fast

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance (Root) (11s): matchup-defining — His lock-on root. Dodge it. Track it before every commit. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call — it changes every dive call.
edits.after: - Twisted Advance (14s at rank 1): his lock-on root, and he is UNTARGETABLE during the dash — don't spend burst into it. - Sapling Toss (18s at rank 1, 1100 range): the zoning tool that decides your CS. - Nature's Grasp (130s at rank 1): a wall that cuts your retreat, and you have no dash. - Your R: kill windows only.

edits.before: Maokai roots with W and sustains with saplings. Dodge the W, anti-heal, and out-scale his low 1v1 threat. Track Twisted Advance (Root) before every step-up.
edits.after: Maokai roots with Twisted Advance and sustains off Sap Magic, which refunds every spell he casts or eats. Buy Grievous Wounds, stay outside Sapling Toss's 1100 range, and out-scale a champion with no real 1v1 threat.

edits.before: Track Maokai’s Twisted Advance (Root) (11s): His lock-on root. Dodge it. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Twisted Advance (14s at rank 1): a lock-on root, and he's untargetable mid-dash — hold your burst until he lands.

notes: Chart flipped to the packet and to its own whys: Maokai owns Levels 1 through First item, Mundo takes 2+ items. Real errors killed: 'Sapling Toss (W... E)' garbled slot (it is E), 'Bramble Smash (W)' (it is Q), and Twisted Advance's cooldown listed as 11s when that is its rank-4 value — rank 1 is 14s. Deleted the advice, in three separate fields, to escape roots with Blunt Force Trauma: Mundo has no dash of any kind, which is exactly why Nature's Grasp cutting the retreat matters. Added the two interactions the page never had: Twisted Advance is untargetable during the dash, so burst spent into it is wasted, and Mundo's passive resists that first root and drops a canister he must walk over.
